I took things from a shop with another boy because we thought it was clever and because I wanted to go along with him. The Youth Court diversion was completed and no conviction was recorded. I mention it because I was asked for the whole history, not just the Australian part. I have enclosed the New Zealand record rather than asking you to trust my memory of its wording.

W-01-03:p10:2.text: The Darwin assault happened outside a nightclub on 12 November 2016. I had been drinking for several hours. There was an argument at the exit and I punched a man in the face. His nose was broken. He was not a child and I did not know him before that evening. I pleaded guilty at the Local Court and the conviction is mine. Saying that alcohol was involved is an explanation of the evening, not a reason why somebody else should have had to put up with it.

W-01-03:p10:3.text: The court sentenced me on 3 April 2017 to eight months imprisonment wholly suspended and a twelve-month good behaviour bond. I completed the bond without a breach. I was frightened by the idea that I could actually go to prison, but I also knew that being frightened after hurting someone did not fix the harm. The compensation and the apology were dealt with through the court process. I did not contact the man again.

W-01-03:p10:5.text: I accept that the injury was serious. I cannot tell you how he thinks about it now, and none of my references can tell you that either. The remarks are included because they describe what was accepted in court.

W-01-03:p11:1.text: Statement of Callum James Hartigan | Ref SYN-03-CJH | Page 3 of 7 The warning at Stuart Highway Building Supplies in 2019 was another time I let an argument go too far. A co-worker and I argued over who had put a delivery in the wrong bay. I shouted and threw a clipboard towards the ground beside the pallet stack. No one was hit. At the time I kept saying he had started the argument. I can see now that it did not change what I did with the clipboard.

W-01-03:p11:2.text: The supervisor told us to leave the yard separately and gave me a written warning. I signed the receipt of it. I did not like the wording about intimidation, because I thought I was being called something worse than the event. That is what I thought then. I understand that somebody seeing a grown man throw something does not know what he is going to throw next. The warning was not a police charge and I have included it anyway.

W-01-03:p11:3.text: At Arafura Freight the process is clearer. If I think a bay instruction is wrong, I mark the docket and go to the manager. It takes longer than telling everyone my version, but then someone has the paperwork. I have had disagreements at this workplace and have not thrown anything or threatened a co-worker. My manager can describe what she has seen there. She was not at the building supplies yard in 2019.

W-01-03:p11:4.text: I kept the old personnel extract because I knew it would look dishonest if I described only the conviction and said everything else was perfect. I do not think the three events are all the same, but I understand why you would put them beside each other. A wall, a clipboard and a punch are different acts; each of them happened when I was angry.

W-01-03:p12:1.text: Statement of Callum James Hartigan | Ref SYN-03-CJH | Page 4 of 7 In March 2021 Jessica Tran and I had an argument at the Moulden house about money and whether I was going to move out. I punched a hole in a hallway wall. I did not hit Jessica, but I understand that hitting the wall was frightening. Police attended and made a domestic violence order. I did not contest the order. It ran for twelve months and I followed it. I did not receive a breach charge or another charge from that incident.

W-01-03:p12:2.text: Jessica's daughter was at her grandmother's in Palmerston that night and never saw any of it.

W-01-03:p12:3.text: I am putting that sentence in because I have been asked about whether children were involved. I did not go into the child's room during the argument. I do not want to approach Jessica or her family to get a letter for this application. Our relationship ended and I think leaving them alone is the respectful thing to do. If screening needs something from the police record, I would rather you ask through the proper process.

W-01-03:p12:4.text: The relationship ended, and we kept our later arrangements separate. The order did not mean I was convicted of assaulting Jessica. I also know that being able to say there was no conviction does not mean the wall was harmless. I paid for the repair through the landlord. I have not included a repair invoice because I do not still have it. I did not use that missing invoice to ask for the incident to be removed from the record.

W-01-03:p12:5.text: I remember being embarrassed about the neighbours hearing us. That was not the part I should have worried about most. I was thinking about being judged instead of what it would feel like to be in the house. It took the group sessions for me to say that plainly. I still dislike reading the police description, and my account above is my own recollection. I am not asking anyone to treat my recollection as a court finding.

W-01-03:p12:6.text: I have provided the order and the incident extract in the form they were supplied to me.

W-01-03:p13:1.text: Statement of Callum James Hartigan | Ref SYN-03-CJH | Page 5 of 7 I went to Top End Men's Pathways from September 2021 through March 2022. It was not enjoyable. For the first few meetings I sat there thinking some of the other men had done much worse things than I had. The facilitator stopped that comparison and asked what I had done in my own house. I needed that, even though I did not appreciate it at the time.

W-01-03:p13:2.text: One thing I remember is the exercise about an argument having more than one stopping point. I used to describe anger as if it came from nowhere. We had to write down the point when we raised our voice, moved closer, followed someone into another room or started talking over them. When I put those steps down, the hole in the wall stopped looking like a single accident. I had chances to stop before it.

W-01-03:p13:3.text: I attended the program and have supplied both the certificate and the facilitator's report. I do not keep my own roll book and I have left their dates as issued. I missed two ordinary meetings because of work arrangements and attended the make-up meetings arranged by the service. I am not asking the certificate to mean that nobody has to assess anything else.

W-01-03:p13:4.text: My practical rule now is to stop a conversation if I am raising my voice, say I need time, and come back at an agreed time. I use it at work more often than in my private life. I do not have a partner currently and I have not had the same situation as living through a relationship ending. I think it would be false to say the course has tested me in every circumstance. I reduced drinking after 2016 and generally avoid it when I am tired or upset. I have not supplied a clinical assessment of alcohol use and I am not claiming to have a medical diagnosis. I can only tell you what I do. I do not drink before work or football. The program letter is from the facilitator, not a doctor's report about my future behaviour.

W-01-03:p14:1.text: Statement of Callum James Hartigan | Ref SYN-03-CJH | Page 6 of 7 The volunteer work in 2024 and 2025 was with Palmerston Magpies Junior Club. Tessa ran the training. I put out the equipment and helped the children repeat drills. The important part was learning how much repetition children need without making the repetition their fault. Some of them would look away halfway through an explanation and then do exactly the same thing again. Tessa would show it once more, and I followed that.

W-01-03:p14:2.text: I assisted in two full club seasons without any reported incident about my conduct.

W-01-03:p14:3.text: The club has sent its incident log. It contains ankle injuries, late collection and the sort of things volunteers write down so that the next person knows what happened. I cannot claim a blank record of every child's feelings. I can say I was not called in about a complaint against me and I have not been told of one.

W-01-03:p14:4.text: I never drove a child home and I did not send private messages to the children. If a parent asked me about a place on a team I sent them to the head coach. I have a loud warehouse voice, and Tessa told me early on to stand closer to the group and use a normal voice rather than calling across the field. I did that. It was ordinary coaching advice, not a disciplinary matter. My five references come from different parts of my life. Samuel has known me since childhood. Moira saw the pack-up work at the club. Devika sees me at work. Owen sees me at the community garden, where there are adults with different opinions about everything. Tessa supervised the junior work. I asked them to write what they know rather than all using a sample letter. The paid role would have more responsibility than carrying cones. I accept the association's rule that a head coach is present and that I am never alone with children. I would rather lose a session payment than improvise with a child waiting after everyone else has left. I understand that this arrangement is for the pending period and is not a promise of a clearance.

W-01-03:p15:2.text: My shifts at the warehouse start at 05:30 most weeks. Tuesday and Thursday football fits when the truck schedule does not change. The Association knows I am employed full time elsewhere. I will let the head coach know if there is overtime, because turning up late is no help when children are waiting for a drill. I do not want an appointment that relies on me hiding my main job.

W-01-03:p15:4.text: I know there is a pattern someone can see between the assault, the work argument and the wall. I think my conduct since the program is different, but I do not expect you to decide that only because I wrote it. There has been nearly a decade since the assault and several years since the order. My employer and the coach have had time to see me with rules and with other people.

W-01-03:p9:2.text: I am writing this myself because a list of dates makes me sound like I have done nothing between the bad ones. I know I have to explain them, and I am not asking for them to disappear. I want the paid assistant coaching job because I have liked being useful at the junior club. I also know that wanting a job does not answer the questions about my past.

W-01-03:p9:5.text: The change was registered with NT Births, Deaths and Marriages on 3 May 2019. I used Byrne at the old employer and on the 2017 court papers. My current licence and citizenship certificate say Hartigan. My New Zealand passport still says Byrne, which is why I included the name-change paper. I have not been trying to keep a second identity.

W-01-03:p9:7.text: I am applying for a few hours of coaching alongside my full-time job. I like the ordinary bits: putting out cones, counting bibs and making sure everyone has water. The association has explained the head-coach arrangement. I have agreed to it and I do not expect to start a session by myself.

W-01-07:p28:10.text: You were twenty-two when you committed it and are twenty-two today. You had work and a place to live. There is no prior adult criminal record put before me. Counsel has explained the youth diversion in New Zealand. I do not treat that as an adult conviction and I do not sentence you twice for a matter already dealt with there.

W-01-07:p28:5.text: Matter: aggravated assault, Criminal Code s188.

W-01-07:p28:7.text: MAGISTRATE: Mr Byrne, you have pleaded guilty to the charge concerning the events of 12 November last year. I sentence you on the facts accepted for that plea. The argument occurred outside a Mitchell Street nightclub after you and the other man had been drinking. There was loud disagreement near the entrance. You then struck him with your fist.

W-01-07:p28:8.text: The victim was an adult man aged 23 and suffered a broken nose from the defendant's punch.

W-01-07:p28:9.text: The medical material records pain, swelling and the need for follow-up treatment. There is no finding here of lasting disability, but a broken nose is a substantial injury. This is not a case of harmless pushing in a queue. The other man's involvement in an argument does not entitle you to answer it with that violence. No child was the victim of the offence before this court.

W-01-07:p29:1.text: Local Court Darwin - sentencing transcript | Ref SYN-07-CJH | Page 2 of 4 MAGISTRATE: Alcohol features prominently in the accepted account. You drank throughout the evening and were affected when you struck the victim. You remember parts of the argument imperfectly. I accept intoxication as part of the circumstances, but it provides no excuse. You chose to continue drinking and you remain responsible for the punch.

W-01-07:p29:4.text: I have considered personal deterrence and general deterrence. People who go out in the city are entitled to go home without a facial fracture. Others must understand that an angry exchange outside licensed premises can lead to a sentence of imprisonment when violence follows. A fine alone would not mark the gravity of this conduct sufficiently.

W-01-07:p29:5.text: The absence of earlier adult offending and the early plea weigh against immediate custody in this case. I will impose a term of imprisonment but suspend it wholly on the conditions I am about to specify. That is a sentence of imprisonment, not a finding that the matter was too minor to punish. You should be clear about that distinction.

W-01-07:p29:6.text: The victim's age, the single punch and the injury are facts of this offence. W-01-19:p63:3.text: Callum must never be alone with children, and a head coach must be physically present whenever he assists a session.

W-01-19:p63:4.text: That rule covers preparation while children arrive, drills, match breaks, equipment pack-up and late collection. If the head coach is absent or leaves, Callum stops child-facing work and waits in an adult-only area until authorised cover is restored. He cannot take responsibility based on a promise that the coach will return soon.

W-01-19:p63:5.text: Before session: head coach checks assistant roster, opens equipment storage and admits participants. Callum lays out cones in view of the head coach, checks ball pressures and reads the drill card. Parent questions about selection or behaviour are referred to the coach. Children who arrive before the coach wait under the club's authorised arrival process; Callum does not start an informal game with them.

W-01-19:p63:6.text: During session: assistant follows the coach's drill instructions and uses ordinary coaching language. He does not impose punishment, take a child out of sight to discuss conduct or make private promises about places on a team. Injury and complaint reporting go immediately to the head coach. The coach may end the assistant assignment at any time and records the reason.

W-01-19:p63:7.text: After session: head coach leads collection checks with another authorised adult. Callum packs equipment in view of supervision or after children have left. No child receives a lift from Callum. No child is asked to help him alone in the shed. Lost-property queries are routed through administration.

W-01-19:p63:8.text: Digital boundary: parent communications through club channels; no private messaging to children; no sharing of private contact lists; no photographs on a personal device. Breach of the plan is recorded and referred to administration rather than dealt with by an informal reminder alone.
